strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing a genuine gap between hard precedence constraints (PSV) and soft weights (WSV), with clear application scenarios
Solid and comprehensive axiomatic characterization that uniquely determines PASV through natural axioms (E+L+NP+M+MS+SCF+WP+EWU)
Principled theoretical framework showing correct reduction to PSV and WSV as special cases with clear explanation of why the |max⪯(Sₜ)| factor is necessary
Efficient and practical MCMC algorithm with local acceptance ratio evaluation (Lemma 4.1) enabling scalable computation on general DAGs
Novel and actionable diagnostic tool (priority sweeping) for practitioners to assess attribution sensitivity and identify unstable contributors
Comprehensive experiments on realistic data lineage scenarios (14-block DAG) and feature attribution with insightful analysis of non-monotone sweeping behavior (Table 3)
Interesting theoretical analysis of limiting regimes with appropriate caveats acknowledged via counterexample (Figure 3)
Clear and well-organized presentation with strong motivation (Figure 1) and accessible mathematical exposition overall
weaknesses: Theoretical contribution is somewhat incremental—combines existing concepts (PSV + weighted sampling) in a principled but relatively natural way
Limited practical guidance for practitioners on specifying inputs: DAGs are constructed ad-hoc (LLM consultation in Appendix B.2.3) and λ weights chosen manually without principled methodology
Experimental validation shows flexibility but lacks evidence of practical superiority; no ground truth or expert validation that PASV produces better attributions than existing methods
Computational efficiency not quantified: no runtime comparisons, MCMC convergence analysis absent, and hyperparameter choices (B=100,000, τ=10,000) used empirically without justification
Limiting regime results (Propositions 3.13–3.14) have significant caveats; general DAGs don't guarantee translation to DAG edges (Figure 3 counterexample), limiting interpretability
Modest experimental scope with relatively small datasets (n=800 data points, n=12 features) and no evaluation of scalability to larger realistic ML applications
Sensitivity to DAG misspecification not explored; no guidance on validating or selecting between alternative DAG specifications empirically
Missing convergence analysis for MCMC algorithm (mixing times, effective sample size diagnostics) and no theoretical complexity guarantees provided

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing real limitations of standard Shapley values in settings with precedence constraints and priority considerations
Rigorous theoretical framework with principled axiomatization showing PASV is uniquely characterized by natural axioms
Elegant theoretical contributions including PROV/SCF framework and limiting case analysis
Solid algorithmic development with efficient MCMC sampler achieving O(n²) mixing time and local acceptance ratio optimization
Comprehensive experimental validation across data valuation and feature attribution tasks with priority sweeping diagnostic
Thorough reproducibility support with detailed implementations, algorithms, and extensive appendices with proofs and additional experiments
Good presentation of technical content overall with clear motivation and well-structured development
weaknesses: Limited practical validation—experiments primarily show PASV *can* differentiate based on weights, not that resulting valuations are superior; no compelling cases where ignoring precedence yields demonstrably wrong results
Incremental technical contributions that combine existing ideas (precedence Shapley, weighted Shapley, MCMC sampling) rather than introducing fundamentally new concepts

Critical practical guidance is missing: no principled methodology for DAG construction (Census Income DAG via ChatGPT raises concerns), no guidance for weight specification (λ = b^c appears arbitrary), no sensitivity analysis to weight misspecification

Scalability concerns for realistic applications—experiments use closed-form utilities or small datasets; proxy-based estimator requires O(n²) memory (tens of GB for n=2048); no experiments with expensive utilities (e.g., deep learning)

Theoretical gaps including lack of intuition for why this hard/soft priority combination is optimal, no sample complexity or convergence rate analysis, and Propositions 3.13-3.14 conditions are quite specific
Limited experimental scope: data valuation only on MNIST/CIFAR10 with k-NN, feature attribution only on Census Income with single architecture, no comparison with other recent data valuation methods

Presentation could be more accessible—dense technical content, axiomatization presented as outline before details, SCF framework notation-heavy without sufficient intuition, figures 5 and 19 difficult to parse

strengths: Well-motivated unification of hard precedence constraints and soft individual weights, addressing real practical needs in data valuation and feature attribution
Rigorous axiomatic characterization with novel State-Choice Factorization concept that elegantly separates global structure effects from individual weighting
Practical contribution of 'priority sweeping' sensitivity diagnostic providing actionable robustness analysis for practitioners
Theoretically sound: clean reduction results showing PSV and WSV as special cases; insightful limiting case analysis (Propositions 3.13-3.14) on extreme weights
Computationally competent: well-designed MCMC Algorithm 1 with efficient local acceptance ratio computation; empirical mixing time O(n²) with limited weight effect
Handles general DAGs (meaningful generalization over WSV's ordered partitions); comprehensive experimental validation with data valuation and feature attribution applications
weaknesses: Conceptual novelty is incremental: core formula (Eq. 4) is straightforward generalization of weighted Shapley to general DAGs; combines existing technical machinery (posets, weighted Shapley, MCMC) rather than introducing fundamentally new ideas

Insufficient baseline comparisons: missing empirical comparison with recent data valuation methods (Beta Shapley, Data Banzhaf, replication-robust variants) cited in paper; only compares against foundational SV/PSV/WSV

Critical practical issues unresolved: DAG construction relies on ChatGPT (Section F.3); no principled procedure for weight λ selection, leaving practitioners with ad-hoc guidance; these gaps limit real-world deployment despite theoretical soundness

Computational complexity analysis incomplete: mixing time analysis primarily empirical without formal guarantees under weighted setting; scalability modest (n≤2048 for proxy method); proxy-based variant requires tens of GB peak memory, raising practical concerns
Experimental scale and scope limited: data valuation uses n=800 points, feature attribution n=12 features; more ambitious experiments needed; limited ablation studies on method sensitivity

Axiomatization section (3.3) is mathematically dense and lacks intuitive explanation; missing worked toy example; U-shaped priority sweep patterns (Section F.4.1) explained post-hoc rather than predicted
